# POSTSEPTAL CELLULITIS (ORBITAL CELLULITIS)

Postseptal cellulitis (orbital cellulitis) is often preceded by sinusitis and requires immediate consultation with otolaryngology and ophthalmology. Urgent surgical drainage may be necessary. The most common pathogenic organisms in adults are streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus aureus.
Contact otolaryngology or ophthalmology immediately for urgent surgical drainage. Broad-spectrum empirical antimicrobials should be used until a pathogen can be identified from the drainage fluid.

## Duration of treatment

Orbital cellulitis should be treated until all signs of infection have resolved. Uncomplicated orbital cellulitis should be treated for minimum of 2 weeks and complicated orbital cellulitis (severe ethmoid sinusitis and bony destruction of sinus) should be treated for at least 4 weeks.

---

References:

- Carlisle et al., American Family Physician. 2015, 92(2)106-112
- Mandell chapter: Periocular infections
- Up-to-Date article: Orbital Cellulitis
- Sanford keyword: Orbital cellulitis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

Preferred:
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 1000 mg IV q12h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

### Step-down treatment after initial intravenous therapy. Base selection on culture results. Adjust duration based on criteria above.

Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID ($) [R] < AND > trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 7 days

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] < AND > trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO q12h ($) [R,DI] for 7 days

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($) [R] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($)
[R]
